description:
Searches file contents with a regular expression and reports the matches. Use it to find where a symbol, string, or pattern occurs, and read the matching file before changing it.

The pattern uses Rust regex syntax, with no look-around and no back-references. Escape ( [ { . when you mean them literally, or set literal to true to match the pattern as plain text. Matching is case-sensitive unless -i is set.

Files are searched in path order, the same order Glob uses: directories are entered depth first, and the names in each directory are in byte order. Output stops at {body_cap} bytes, and at most 100000 files are considered in one search. A file over {file_ceiling} bytes is not searched. Binary files, symbolic links, over-size files, and entries that cannot be read are skipped, and the result says how many were skipped and why.

Only entries named .git are skipped, and .gitignore rules are not applied, so output such as target/ and node_modules/ is searched when it lies under path. Narrow path, glob, or type to keep it out.

In content mode each match line is shown as N:text and each context line as N-text, under the absolute path of its file. The N and the colon or hyphen are not part of the line, and N is the line number Read shows. A line over 1000 bytes is shown as a window around its first match, with markers that give the bytes left out.

Paths in the result are absolute and work as the path argument of the other file tools.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in, as an absolute path. Defaults to the run's filesystem root.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files, for example "*.js" or "**/*.tsx". Only * and ** are special, and matching is case-sensitive. A pattern that does not start with "/" is matched at any depth. A pattern that starts with "/" is a full path.

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "content".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match. Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match. Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-C.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match. Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

type.description: File type to search. Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than glob for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries. Works across all output modes: content (limits matching lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Pass 0 for no limit, which is also what leaving it out means.

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit. Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines. Default: false.

literal.description: Match the pattern as plain text instead of as a regular expression, so ( [ { . and the rest need no escape. Default: false.
